# The Quiet Library

By *Ada Reader*, 12 March 2025

Libraries have always been places of **quiet** work. This guide walks through the reading rooms, the stacks, and the small rituals that keep a good library running. For more background see [the history of reading rooms](https://example.org/history) and the [online catalog](https://example.org/catalog).

## Reading rooms

The main reading room holds two hundred desks. Each desk has a lamp, a power outlet, and a small shelf for notes. Staff ask visitors to keep conversation to a whisper.

> A library is not a luxury but one of the necessities of life.
>
> Henry Ward Beecher

### Opening hours

| Day | Opens | Closes |
|-----|-------|--------|
| Monday | 09:00 | 18:00 |
| Saturday | 10:00 | 16:00 |
| Sunday | Closed | Closed |

## What to bring

- A valid library card
- Pencil and paper (pens are not allowed near rare books)
- Headphones for the listening booths

1. Sign in at the front desk
2. Collect a locker key
3. Find your desk

![A long room with rows of wooden desks and green lamps](reading-room.jpg)

## Catalog commands

Staff use a short command to look up a title:

```
find --title "Quiet"
  --author "Reader"
  --limit 10
```

### Closing note

Thank you for keeping the library quiet. Questions? Email [the front desk](mailto:desk@example.org).
